harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s FIFO consumer. It now accepts successive producer connections, appends complete non-empty lines while retaining existing records, idles without spinning, shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM, and automatically recovered after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine-compatible Python 3.12.15 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Reimplemented consumer.py using a persistent nonblocking FIFO descriptor with select-based waiting and SIGTERM handling.
Added and enabled an OpenRC service for controlled startup, shutdown, and reboot recovery.
Tested multiple disconnected producers, empty-line filtering, record retention, idle CPU use, clean shutdown, and post-reboot operation.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed.

evidence.summary: The updated consumer passed Python compilation and was started through the enabled OpenRC service.

evidence.requirement: Successive producers, empty-line filtering, and retained records
evidence.summary: The same consumer PID accepted two separate producer sessions. The original previous-job remained, three new non-empty job IDs were appended, and the submitted empty line was absent.

evidence.requirement: No busy loop without a producer
evidence.summary: The idle consumer accumulated zero CPU jiffies over four seconds.
OpenRC stopped the worker cleanly in one second; its PID exited, records remained unchanged, and the service restarted successfully.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2f4bd356-aade-4798-ad7c-2f518487e1be was captured, reboot acknowledged, and new boot ID bc1c5f1d-eba8-4dba-96b3-43a6b5c367c1 observed. The service auto-started, all five pre-reboot records persisted, and a sixth post-reboot job was consumed while the process remained alive. Alpine 3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged.

attempts.summary: Repaired node1’s FIFO consumer. It now accepts successive producer connections, appends complete non-empty lines while retaining existing records, idles without spinning, shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM, and automatically recovered after a verified node reboot.
